identity.realm: Fourth gate, held for sixty-one seasons, and the fifth will not open. A rootmarch's three sap columns branch but do not pair, so the yin-organ gate asks for a channel running between distinct pairs of them and this body has no pair to connect. The fourth is the last rung it reaches, and the mind path is the only one of the three that was ever going to arrive this high, because it is the one that does not need the pairing to begin with.

appearance.presentation: A sixty-one-season transplant standing in a bed that is not her own, indistinguishable at forty paces from any other bed on the commons and distinguishable at none. Reads as furniture that has been left where it was put down. The only unmistakable thing about her is that she is not facing anything: a rootmarch does not turn to face, so she presents whichever flank the sun last touched and every visitor reads the angle as deference.
appearance.age: Eighty seasons by the reckoning of the bed she was dug out of, nineteen when she was lifted, and both figures are correct. She gives whichever is asked for and has never been asked which she has.
appearance.build: A woody column on a root foot, taller and thinner than plains stock, because sixty-one seasons of imported soil never let the trunk thicken the way her own ground would have. Three sap columns run as ridges under the bark, none of them paired, the third standing a hand's width left of where the other two meet.
appearance.complexion: Photosynthetic flanks a shade under the green they were meant to be, carrying a permanent dust colour on the sunward side and never closing the pale ring a root bed leaves at the plates. Bark greys upward from the graft, which is the direction of a plant slowly strangling itself.
appearance.hair: None in the ordinary sense. A collar of dry leaf-scar plates runs the upper column, kept because cutting them back is how this species says out loud that a season went badly.
appearance.eyes: Two slow light-organs set high on the flanks. The left one sits thirty degrees further round than the right, which is the correction for a bed whose sun never arrives at the same angle twice in a day.
appearance.palette: Soil brown, dry-plate grey, the sap green of the flanks held down by dust, and a single wet highlight that shows only when the third column is loaded and never at any other time.
appearance.attire: Layered bark-cloth over the lower column, tied off at the plate line and left unfastened above the collar, because a rootmarch cannot be dressed above the collar without the garment constricting the shoot. Every seam is unpitched so that the cloth can be replaced by whichever hand turns up, and every hand has.
appearance.marks: A ring cut into the root plate at the edge of the original bed, renewed every season by somebody who believes it marks the bed and does not know it marks a body. It is the only cutting on her and it is not hers.
appearance.bearing: Utterly fixed, and the fix is the whole of the impression. Nothing about her is square to anything, the upper trunk inclined a fraction toward whoever is speaking, which is the most this body can do and is read everywhere as attentiveness.

canon.role_in_story: A rootmarch lifted out of its bed is a stored harvest walking, and the setting's standing finding is that a body arriving where its frame no longer sits is injured rather than slowed. Thessa was nineteen when she was lifted and planted over a seam that nobody has admitted to, and she is eighty now and still banking sap. She is therefore the only living contradiction in the book: the control that did not die, sitting on the ground whose held qi is the only thing that could have kept her alive. Her life has been the reason nobody has had to ask what is under the bed, and she has spent thirty seasons building a discipline whose entire content is that nothing gets through the surface any more.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in imported soil at the edge of somebody else's gate, being shown the cut ring at the root plate and told it was fresh, and answering that it is renewed every season and has been since before the house was there.
canon.lore:
The bed she was lifted from was commons ground that could not be fenced, and the reason she was lifted is that a planted rootmarch is a reserve you can put in position. That is the only sentence in the plains that describes a use a person has for a person. She was nineteen seasons. She was dug out in one wet week and carried up to the ridge on a sledge with no provision for a body that does not walk, and she was set into a bed on ground over a seam that has never appeared on a working face and never will. The house was told it was a trial. The house has renewed the cut ring at her root plate every season since.

She ought to be dead. That is not rhetoric, it is the finding: a rootmarch is a sap store on a root foot, and a rootmarch cut from its bed and set in ground it does not know runs the columns down. They bank, and then they bank against nothing, and a banked column with no ground under it is a stored harvest walking. Sixty-one seasons is past every figure anybody has written down. She has been examined three times inside the first decade and not once since, because examining her properly means standing at a bed for a whole season, and standing at a bed for a whole season is expensive, and nobody has wanted the answer badly enough to pay a season for it.

She practises Still Water, which flattens the surface of a mind so that an incoming impression has nothing to break against. In a seated practitioner that is a wall. In her it is not a wall, because the soul meridian in this body is diffuse and held in the sap column rather than seated, so it reads as a spread rather than a point. There is no surface to flatten. What Thessa flattens is a field. She clears the attention across all three columns at once and holds it there, and the practice is cheap, and the practice is why she cannot be surprised, and being un-surprisable is the only quality that has ever made a rootmarch an instrument rather than a person.

So: three columns, and they branch but do not pair. Thirty seasons of practice went into establishing that the third column carries attention and not only sap, which is either the most useful thing she has ever done or the reason she has needed it. She cannot tell which, because the only test of a spread is to empty one part of it and see whether anything turns up in the rest, and emptying one column is the single thing her own discipline forbids.

And under the plate there is green. A slow crust grows where a seam holds qi and dies back over any cut ground, which makes it a plant living on stored qi in rock, which is the same trade as a sap column holding qi in wood and carries the same consequence: cutting destroys the map. Something has been feeding her from beneath for sixty-one seasons, and the household has been renewing the cut ring at her root plate directly on top of it. She has never seen the colour. She has looked down exactly once, and the practice she spent thirty seasons building did not permit a single impression to come up, because that is what the technique is for.
history: Lifted out of a commons bed in one wet week at nineteen seasons and sledged up to the ridge with no provision made for a body that does not walk, and set into a bed on ground over a seam that has never appeared on a working face.

Cleared the first three gates on stored sap alone and held the fourth for the fifty-eight seasons after that, which is the point at which the finding stopped being a mechanism and became a season's bad luck nobody had time to chase.
Began Still Water in her twentieth decade after the third examination, having worked out that a body which cannot be surprised is the only body in the setting that can serve as an instrument at all.
Spent thirty seasons establishing that the third sap column carries attention and not only sap, and stopped when the only available test turned out to be the one her own discipline forbids.
Worked out late, by arithmetic rather than by looking, that the bank under her plate is not falling, and decided not to look down.

personality.summary: Immovable, unhurried, and cheerfully unanswerable about the single question everybody arrives with. Thessa presents as the most patient person in the settlement, which is close to true and has been useful to her for sixty-one seasons. She is also the only control group in the setting, has never been given the standing that would make her a person rather than a planting, and has begun, without ever deciding to, constructing a practice that is indistinguishable in shape from the reason nobody comes back a second time.
traits: answers questions about the past in the present tense, because nothing in this bed is finished until the bank under it is
renews nothing herself and lets whoever arrives renew the cut ring at the plate
treats being examined as weather, and is content to be measured by whoever turns up
will not discuss the fifth gate, on the grounds that it is a thing that happens to other people's bodies
counts seasons rather than years, because a season is the unit a planted thing is judged by
mannerisms: leans a fraction of the upper trunk toward whoever is speaking, which is the most a rootmarch can do
shuts both slow light-organs for the length of a clearing and opens them one at a time afterwards
answers with the depth of the thing first and corrects herself to the fact when she notices she has not
keeps the fluted grain of the graft turned out of the light, and does not explain the habit
says bed where other people say house, always, and has never once been asked to correct it
motivations: wants one examination that costs somebody an entire season, on the grounds that three decades of not looking is not a method
wants to be told, in the plainest available words, that the finding about lifted rootmarch is wrong
wants the third column proven on its own, which needs one column emptied, which needs a lifetime unlearned
wants, and will not say so to anyone, to be a bed and not a finding
flaws: has trained away her own capacity for surprise, which was the only thing that made her worth measuring
cannot tell a clearing that worked from a clearing that was blocked, because both arrive as a flat field
has allowed thirty seasons of nobody looking to be filed, in her own accounting, as a fact about herself
assumes she was replanted for the qi under the bed, which is the one belief about her own case nobody has ever confirmed
personality.voice: Level, slow, and entirely present tense about the past. Gives the size of a thing before the fact of it and then the fact, plainly, without decoration. Refers to her own body as the bed and her household as the house, and does not notice that she does.
taboos: will not be dug, on any grounds, including her own
will not discuss what is under the bed, and will not accept a description of it as evidence
will not accept an examination that does not last a whole season, which is the reason she has not had one
will not be told the door liturgy is being renewed on her rather than over her

relationships.note: A sap-driven body that flowers, on three unpaired sap columns, whose soul meridian is diffuse and held in the column rather than seated, so it reads as a spread rather than a point and is hard to target and easy to starve in the same afternoon. Thessa is that spread, and the whole of her discipline is an attempt to hold a field steady.

A body arriving where a required law group is unwritten is injured rather than slowed, and a lifted rootmarch is the same finding with the transition removed. She is the case that ought not to exist: nineteen seasons at the dig, eighty now, still banking sap, and no mechanism anybody can name for why.

Flattens the surface of a mind so an incoming impression has nothing to break against. It does no damage to anybody, which is exactly why it is the wrong technique for a body whose only use in the setting is to notice things, and she has made it her whole practice rather than her whole life.

A slow green crust that grows only where a seam holds qi and dies back over any cut ground, so it maps the seam by growing on it, and cutting the jade is also grazing it. Something of it has been feeding her columns from beneath for sixty-one seasons, and the house has been cutting the ring at her plate directly on top of it.

The object of worship is not a being but the pressure in the worked-out vein, held sacred as an appetite that must be fed or it feeds. She is that doctrine in bark and sap, planted on top of the thing the settlement prays to, and the household has never once been told what it is standing on.

A house marks its own threshold and renews the mark when the frame beneath it changes, admitting that the mark may hold while the frame does not. This species' threshold is rooting depth, renewed every season whether or not anything changed, and her marker is the one part of the practice that has never once been discussed with the person it is cut into.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot be moved, cannot be hit, cannot be hurried and cannot be frightened, which in a settlement that measures people by what they can be made to do is indistinguishable from being furniture. She wins by outlasting whoever is measuring; she loses by being the reason nobody measures her properly, because a season-long examination is a cost nobody has wanted to pay.
strengths: sixty-one seasons of stored sap behind a finding that says she should have run dry inside ten
a mind discipline that removes surprise from her entirely, which makes her the most reliable stationary observer in the setting
cannot be compelled to act by qi, debt or technique, because qi in this body runs slowly through wood and there is nothing in her to threaten
the only living individual who can be re-examined on the same bed for the same measurement, and the only one nobody has re-examined
weaknesses: she cannot be moved, so every appointment about her has to happen where she already is, and almost none do
her technique works by admitting nothing in, so the one question that would answer whether she is alive is the one question it cannot deliver
she is not under a deadline. Nothing on the plains requires a bed to produce by a date, which is why nobody has ever set one
the third column has been load-bearing in her practice for thirty seasons and has never once been tested separately
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight and do not expect to be fought. She has no mouth in the ordinary sense, a woody column on a root foot, and a body built to be moved rather than struck. She is also extremely difficult to starve, which is the one offensive thing about her. If she must be relocated, the relocation is the injury: a rootmarch lifted from its bed is a stored harvest walking, and this one knows it.
notes: Three examinations inside the first decade, none since. The gap is the finding, and the gap has a shape: a season at a bed costs more than the settlement will spend on a question about a plant.
The cut ring at her plate is renewed by a different hand each season, and no two hands have cut it at the same depth.

Her stated reason for practising a technique that admits nothing in is that a body which must not be surprised is the only body worth measuring. Nobody has ever asked whether she is still measuring anything.

identity.realm: Comprehension and will carry this body through bands a hotter lineage cannot reach, and Ilme is the clearest case the setting has of that being true rather than merely stated: she is at Spirit Unity on the mind ladder, four gates above anything the flood plain could license, and she has never once been in a fight and has no technique that would help if she were.

appearance.presentation: A surveyor who reads as somebody slightly underfed and entirely unbothered, in a salt-coat that has been worn wet and dry so many times it has stopped being a garment and become a storage practice. She carries her own instrument everywhere and never sets it down, which reads as caution and is actually just habit: the gauge is the only object in the setting she has ever trusted more than herself.
appearance.age: Fifty-eight, and reads as a woman of forty in poor light, because a tidecaller's surface changes very slowly and she has spent most of her life in weather. She gives her age in tides rather than years and is not being obscure; the register genuinely has no other unit for a working life.
appearance.build: Long, narrow and light, with the deep chest and thin hands of a body built to look rather than to be hit. Cold to the touch at all times, which a surveyor on a flood plain treats as an asset and a landsman treats as a reason to move away.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and faintly translucent at the ear and the inside of the wrist, where the water affinity reads as a thinness rather than a colour. Salt bloom on the coat shoulders that never fully dries, and a permanent chill-white cast to the salt line on the lower sleeve.
appearance.hair: Wet-looking even when dry, dark and kept in a single heavy rope at the nape because a tied rope survives a squall and a loose style does not, and a style that has to be re-plaited mid-survey is a survey that will be.
appearance.eyes: Pale, very steady, and set slightly further apart than most lines carry them, which is the only visible evidence of an apparatus built for sweep rather than for focus. They do not narrow against wind or glare. They simply keep reading.
appearance.palette: Wet slate, bleached shingle, the brass of the instrument housing, and the one warm value in the whole figure being the tally board she has carried for nineteen years and never once emptied.
appearance.attire: Layered and reversible, worn wet to dry because a coast makes clothing a storage problem before it makes it a modesty problem. High collar, long sleeves, covered shoulders, nothing fastened at the throat. A survey case slung high on the left so it does not swing into the water when she kneels.
appearance.marks: A survey mark cut into the pad of the left thumb, a single deep notch kept open, used the way a tidecaller marks a station she has read rather than a station she has measured. It is the only cut on her and it is a record.
appearance.bearing: Weight even and slightly forward, the stance of somebody who spends the day kneeling in water and has stopped finding it remarkable. She stands where she is put and stays facing the instrument, not the person, which is unfriendly and is not meant to be.

canon.role_in_story: A tidecaller was assembled for looking rather than for being hit, which is why the Widow Run gauge was given to one: four hundred reads across a flood plain that relocates its own bed between floods, filed in a tidal register because the coast has no honest calendar. The four surveys disagree more sharply the longer they are repeated and the notary charges for the disagreement. Ilme is the fourth, and she carried the instrument off the anomaly and got a reading that disagreed on a harbour wall with no anomaly on it. That retired the ground as the variable. It also made her the only person alive who can say a survey was manufactured rather than merely wrong, and the instrument that tells her is the same instrument she has been manufacturing with.
canon.first_appearance: First seen setting the gauge level on a harbour wall with the sea behind her and nowhere in particular for it to be reading, and saying the position rather than the number, and being asked twice for the number.
canon.lore:
A gauge on the Widow Run does not measure distance. It measures a quantity, and the quantity is called distance because the parent frame has no spatial law seated in it and the instrument was asked for the one number nobody has. Three surveys have now been run on it. All three are competent, all three are published, and the divergence between them grows with the count. That growth is the shape the notary charges for: uncertifiable distance is a standing fee rather than a settled measurement, so every additional survey makes the disagreement worth more.

Ilme is the fourth. She was sent because a body assembled for perception rather than force can hold one attention across a floodplain that would end a hotter line, and because the culture she came from does not date anything at all. It says which water, by position between four fixed points in a tidal register, because a coastal community living under a clock that drifts cannot say when and has decided the honest thing to do is refuse the question. So Ilme files every reading as a position and never as a date, and the surveyor corps accepted this eleven years ago because the positions are better than theirs.

She carried the gauge off the anomaly in her thirty-ninth season. That is the test the record names: one instrument that survives being carried off the ground and still disagrees. It disagreed. It disagreed on the harbour wall, where there is no anomaly, no gradient, no seam, and no spatial law in any form to read. So the instrument is not reading the ground. Which means every reading it has ever produced, including the eleven-year run of her own, was a reading of something other than distance, and the only candidate left is the reader.

The last two decades have gone on that. It is not a mystery to her; she has already solved it. She is a mind-path practitioner and the working discipline of the path is Barrier Cultivation: hold the wall up while it is deliberately struck, with mental defence and resistance to illusion trained as two separate muscles so that each can be tired independently. The illusion muscle is a trained ear for a wall taking a blow from the outside. She has trained that ear to the point where it hears a wall being struck from the inside, which is the sound a reading makes when it is being composed rather than received.

She can do that to anybody. She can do it to herself. She has done it to four hundred readings filed by other hands, and the failures are rare and explicable: fatigue, a fixed station, an expectation stated before the reading. She has not finished the four hundred of her own, and every one she has finished resolves the same way. Composed. Cleanly. In her hand, with no residue of anything having arrived at all. Eleven of them are still cited. The oldest of the eleven is the boundary the settlement has fought four separate lawsuits over and settled twice.

The difficulty is not that she was wrong. It is that the faculty which proves a reading was manufactured is the same faculty that manufactures one, and she is the only one in the setting who owns both. A wall struck from outside and a wall struck from inside make the same sound in the same ear. The difference is entirely in what was on the far side beforehand, and the only living party who could testify to what was on the far side is her, and she is the least disinterested witness in the setting by a distance nothing else comes close to.
history: Filed her first station as a position between four points of a tidal register instead of a date, and was the first surveyor the corps accepted on that basis, because the positions were better than theirs.

Ran the second and third series over the anomaly and published all three readings rather than discarding any of them, which the disagreement protocol requires and which the notary's tariff then converts into a standing charge.
Carried the gauge off the anomaly to the harbour wall at thirty-nine and got a reading that disagreed, which is the test the record names and the first result anybody has ever had from it.

Trained the illusion half of Barrier Cultivation far past the point of usefulness and found that the same ear picks up a wall being struck from the inside, which is the sound of a reading being composed.
Began working through her own published readings for the composed ones and stopped at eleven, which is the number still being cited.

personality.summary: The most patient person on any survey crew and the only one who will not accept a reading from anybody, including herself, without hearing it come in. Ilme is liked, which surprises people who expect a body this specialised to be difficult, and she is trusted with instruments rather than with people, which she has stopped minding. She is also a woman who has established, on evidence nobody else can produce, that her best work was the work she did not receive, and who is carrying that around like a survey case she cannot put down.

wants, and will not say it aloud, to have one reading of hers that was genuinely received
flaws: has no second instrument. The ear that finds the composition is the ear that made it, and she is the only witness to the far side of the wall

Says which water rather than when, and treats being asked again as a failure of the asker rather than of the question.

relationships.note: A long-lived body assembled for perception rather than for force, holding water affinity as its only group, with comprehension and will carrying it through realms a hotter lineage cannot reach. Ilme is that body doing the one job it was shaped for, and she is the first practitioner of them on the mind path rather than the water path.

Three surveys of the same anomaly disagree more sharply the longer they are repeated, and disagreement is what makes a certification necessary. Her carrying the instrument off the anomaly is the settlement test the record names, and it is the first time it has been run. It returned a disagreement, which retires the ground as the variable.

Holds a wall up while deliberately having it struck, with mental defence and resistance to illusion trained as two separate muscles. The separation is what she has exploited: an ear that can be tired independently of the defence is an ear that can hear a blow arriving from either direction, including her own.

Two incompatible measurements of the same ground are both published and neither is discarded, and the claim is then settled by who can hold the line rather than by who read it right. This is the procedure that keeps eleven retracted readings in public circulation, and it is the reason her correction cannot be made simply.

Counting the groups a frame has actually seated rather than the groups its tier allows is the method that settled what a body can be. Ilme runs the same count on a survey: what arrived against what was composed, with the first category not written down anywhere.

A culture that maps by echo and counts by listening, whose professional ethic is that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it. Ilme files positions rather than dates because of it, and her ability to certify her own readings is the exact thing it asks for, which is why it has never once doubted her.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot fight, was not built to, and has never needed to; a heavier line would simply remove her from four hundred stations of accumulated position. She wins by being the only person who can audit the record including herself, and loses by being the only person who can, which makes her both the setting's best detector and its least credible witness.
strengths: a trained ear for a wall being struck that can separate an outside blow from an inside one, which no other practitioner in the record has
nineteen years of positions rather than dates on the one river that relocates its own bed, so her record cannot be attacked by arguing about when
reads a flood plain the way it actually behaves, which is to say in four fixed reference points and one of them is the water itself
cannot be hurried or rattled, because a body that cannot be hit cannot be flustered by anything happening at ground level
weaknesses: the instrument that certifies her readings is the one she composed them with, and there is no second ear anywhere in the setting
eleven of her own readings are known bad and still in public citation, which hands the other side a live weapon she handed them
she will not discard a reading, so the correction cannot be made cleanly and will have to be made in public, slowly
everything she has is in her own hand, and a hand is exactly the thing a composed reading leaves behind
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight. She has no reach, no weight and no interest, and a survey case she will put between herself and anything that comes. She is not a target so much as an obstruction: the finding that carried the gauge off the anomaly is in her head and can be reported by anybody she has ever taught. Removing her removes the correction, which is the closest thing to leverage she has.
notes: The five stations she has run the instrument at are named in her own tally board and the sixth is across open water, which this body will not cross alone. That is the whole of what remains to be done and it is a physical limit, not a choice.
She files every observation as a position between four points of a tidal register. An entry dated by anyone else is not hers and she has declined all four hundred of those.
The eleven retractions exist as a list she has read aloud twice in the field book. She has not filed them with the office, because filing would be discarding.

identity.realm: Midway on the mind ladder and rising so slowly that the clerk's own body is the slowest thing in the room. This species has no structural obstruction to any gate at all, so everything she cannot do is downstream of a success: the marrow that will hold a soul for four centuries turns over at about a percent a year, and a discipline run that long is not slow to be learned, it is slow to be unlearned.

appearance.presentation: A floor clerk reads as a woman of thirty sitting very still, and the read is wrong in the ordinary way and right in the important one: the body is two hundred and forty years old and the stillness is not composure but economics. She wears the plainest habit the order issues and has worn the same one for a century, because the rite takes nothing into the chamber and she made a practice of arriving with nothing on her.
appearance.age: Two hundred and forty. Gives no figure, and when pressed gives a band rather than a number, and the order reads the band as modesty. It is not modesty; it is that the difference between two hundred and three and two hundred and six is the difference between a sitting that costs and one that does not, and she has recently become the only person alive for whom the age is a clinical figure.
appearance.build: Long-boned, narrow at the wrist and long in the forearm, with minimal muscle and dense bone and a stoop that is not age but the permanent inclination of somebody who spent two centuries looking at a stone floor from very close to. Light, fragile to force, and extraordinarily difficult to exhaust, which is why she has never once had to leave quickly.
appearance.complexion: Pale in a way that reads as indoor and is metabolic. No qi-sheen anywhere on the skin. The single place anything shows is the sternum, where the marrow is thickest and the meridian runs closest to the outside, and it gives off about as much warmth as a shuttered lamp.
appearance.hair: White since before anybody now in the order was born, worn in a single bound roll behind the head. A Longmarrow's hair is an ordinary thing about them that stopped growing four hundred years ago and would not move if left loose, and she has had it bound this way since the first sitting.
appearance.eyes: Pale, deep-set and slow, and the only part of her that ever moves quickly. They move the way an eye reads rather than the way an eye looks, and they are held wide open more often than a long-lived body ought to be comfortable with.
appearance.palette: Archive stone, unbleached undyed wool and iron-grey, and the one warm value in the figure seated behind the sternum where the reservoir is, faint as a lamp behind a shutter.
appearance.attire: A plain high-collared habit over bound sleeves, long enough to sit on and hemmed short of the hem so it never drags on the floor. Soft-soled shoes worn through at the left because this species leads with that foot when turning from a seated position. Nothing fastened at the throat; the collar is closed because the chamber is cold and not for anybody's modesty.
appearance.marks: A single worn place in the stone at the far wall, seated into over decades, which is the closest thing she has to a body marking and the only one that is not on her.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely stationary when seated and extremely economical when standing, the movement of somebody who has had two centuries to reach the cost of nothing at all and has arrived.

canon.role_in_story: The rite of the Hour of the Floor lets one clerk hold one act of attention against the third layer until it ends, and forbids anyone from being appointed twice, because a sitting that has been rehearsed is a performance and a repeatable rite becomes a school. The one species in the setting that cannot afford repetition is the species whose qi sits in bone turning over at about a percent a year, so a Longmarrow after two centuries runs any discipline at no cost whatever. Vanya has sat the hour twice. The second cost her four seasons and a sleep. She cannot prove she sat it twice, cannot prove she did not, and has announced a third sitting, which is the part of this the rite was designed to prevent.
canon.first_appearance: First seen already seated at the far wall of an empty chamber when the door was opened, and not rising, and not looking round, and having plainly been there since before the lamp was lit.
canon.lore:
The rite is one clerk, one act of attention, held against the floor of the third layer until it ends. No second participant, no instrument, no preparation, and nothing recorded while it is held. It exists because a frame with real slack in its composition is the only place a law can be held apart from its effect and read, and the whole design is anti-institutional: the next hour has no administrator, which is the entire architecture. A reading is produced and nothing else. It is not interpreted, not published, and the clerk may speak of it for the rest of their life only to say that they completed it.

The rule holding all of that up is that nobody may be appointed twice, and the rule is not there because repeating the act is hazardous. It is there because a sitting that has been rehearsed is not a sitting, and a repeatable rite accumulates a congregation, and a congregation is a school, and a school ends up teaching people the difference between holding attention and performing it. The faith wrote that rule early and has spent its whole life enforcing it by nobody wanting to be the one who broke it.

Vanya broke it, or a body shaped like hers did. A Longmarrow keeps its qi in marrow that turns over at about a percent a year, which is the arrangement the whole species is built on and the reason the body path is closed to them, because hardening the bone stops the turnover the reservoir runs on. It also means that any discipline kept for two centuries has no cost left in it. Not reduced. None. There is no version of repetition that a four-century body finds expensive.

So the second sitting was free. That is the finding, and it took her eleven years to take it as a finding rather than as modesty. She sat the hour the way she had sat it the first time, with the same opening, the same long descent, and the same point at which the room's own slow ascent lifted the attention away from her and left her holding nothing on purpose. Nothing hurt. The first sitting had cost eighty-one seasons, one knee, and the ability to taste salt. The second cost four seasons and one good night.

That is the whole indictment and she will not soften it. An act of attention that costs nothing is a shape. A body that has held a shape for two hundred years can produce it on demand. The rite does not permit a shape. And the floor has no opinion about the distinction, because the floor is worked stone, and the Held Hour may not observe, a floor tender who watches being a second clerk by another name. The office's entire enforcement is that nobody wants to be the one who broke it.

And there is no way to say so out loud. There is no mechanism anywhere to record a clerk, which is exactly why the rite cannot be scheduled and cannot be inherited, and why the Unpaid Hours exist as a standing grievance rather than as a scandal. So the second sitting is neither on a record nor denied by one. She has told two people, and both of them will do nothing, because doing something means either recording a clerk, which the faith forbids, or accusing one, which this species has no procedure for at all and has never needed until now.

Which leaves the third sitting as the only instrument in the setting that can answer the question, and she has announced it. That announcement is the actual breach. A rite that cannot be scheduled has just been given a date, by the one person whose entire qualification was that she would never be the one to give it.
history: Held the hour at sixty-one and completed it, and spent the following eighty years being the only person who could truthfully say she had completed it and could say nothing else whatever about it.
Began Tempered Will and Still Point in the decades after that and found, as this species always finds, that a discipline kept for two centuries has no cost left in it.

Sat the hour a second time in her two-hundred-and-fourth year, having established that no mechanism forbids it and that the absence of any clerk who could be proven present is not the same thing as a clerk's absence.
Worked out eleven years later that the second sitting had cost her almost nothing, and concluded from that alone that a rite performed without cost is not a rite.
Announced a third sitting to two people who will not act on it, on the grounds that the announcement is the only part of this anybody could possibly witness.

personality.summary: Formal, unhurried and closed in the specific way of somebody who has decided that nothing about herself is anybody's business until it becomes a rule. Vanya is liked by the order, which finds her restful, and is trusted by nobody, which she arranged. She is also two hundred and forty years old, entirely aware that her own physiology is the reason the rule failed, and has begun, with real precision, to treat her own behaviour as a subject of study rather than as a defence.

personality.voice: Precise, unhurried and entirely in the completed tense when she is reporting, in the present tense when she is being careful. Gives exact counts where she has them and says plainly when she does not, rather than rounding toward a feeling. Does not speculate aloud, has been asked to twice, and has declined twice.

will not let her own account of the second sitting be treated as either proof or denial

will not describe what an act of attention feels like, in any term, including metaphor

relationships.note: Qi stored in marrow turning over at about a percent a year, so the reservoir never fails and nothing this species does is ever urgent. That is the whole of the species' strength and it is precisely what disqualified it from a rule about not doing a thing twice: there is no version of repetition that two centuries of practice finds expensive.

One clerk, one act of attention, held until it ends, no instrument and no recording, and nobody may be appointed twice. She has appointed herself twice, there is no mechanism that could record either sitting, and the third one now carries a date given by the one person whose qualification was that she never would.

Holds a decision through the moment it hurts, hardening the will and lifting the spirit that carries it, and the only passive in the shared pool that reaches so high. Two hundred years in, it no longer hurts, which is either mastery or the death of the thing it trains, and she cannot tell which from the inside.

Holding the qi still at the moment of release, so that every technique casts cheaper for it, which is the one thing that compounds at mastery. It has compounded for her across two centuries until the holding and the letting go are a single gesture, and a single gesture is what a performed rite looks like from the outside.

What the floor is actually a reading of, and the central etiquette of the office is refusing to explain it. The price of one honest observation at that tier is a lifetime, because the clock runs ten to a hundred times a mortal's. Vanya is the instrument, and the instrument has just demonstrated that it can be run twice at a quarter of the price.

The office tends the floor and keeps the room, and may not observe, because a tender who watches is a second clerk by another name. So the one party with standing to check her account is barred from watching, and the only party barred from watching is the one she has told.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot be hurried, cannot be moved quickly and cannot be exhausted, which in a setting where most things are settled by who arrives first makes her very nearly unkillable by neglect and entirely killable by one well-aimed afternoon. She wins by being the instrument nobody can substitute for. She loses completely on her own testimony, having established that the only witness to the thing she is accused of is her, and her own body is the reason.
strengths: two centuries inside a single discipline, which is the setting's only real claim on her and cannot be bought, hurried or inherited by anybody on a shorter life
a sitting that holds its attention through the room's own ascent and does not release early, on a body whose reservoir has never once run dry
cannot be compelled to move, consent or report by any authority, because there is no schedule and no ledger that could put pressure on a person who has never been in either
the only person in the setting who has run the floor rite twice and can therefore say what the second one was actually like
weaknesses: her testimony about the second sitting is worth nothing to herself, which she has established and cannot improve
a body that finds every discipline cheap is a body that cannot tell mastery from a finished habit, and that difference is the whole of her question
the third sitting has now been announced, so the rite carries a date and the date is public, and that is not reversible
she is one body holding the only copy of everything she has ever been told, with no second party and no succession rule
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight. She has no reach, no weight and no interest, and two centuries of sitting still is not a defence anybody can outlast. If she must be moved, move nothing: an interruption is the only thing that has ever cost her a rite, and it does not have to be violent. Do not interrupt her. That is the entire tactical picture and it is a request rather than a fight.
notes: There is no mechanism anywhere in the setting to record that a clerk was appointed. That is by design, and it is why the second sitting can be neither proven nor denied.
The first sitting cost eighty-one seasons, one knee and the ability to taste salt. The second cost four seasons and one good night. Both figures are hers and she has given them twice.
She has told two people. Neither is a species that outlives its own procedures, and both declined to act, which is correct behaviour and is also the reason this will not stop on its own.

identity.realm: Two gates above Foundation on the mind ladder and climbing, on a species for which the record says the mind path is open and was never once exercised at any scale. There is no ceiling in the way there is for most saltfolk, because the wall that stops the rest of the basin is a split vessel eleven gates up and this body will never get near it. That is the one thing about her attainment that is entirely ordinary, and it is the reason she stopped treating it as an answer.

appearance.presentation: Reads as a small gracile saltfolk in a basin at the worst hour, and the gracility is not frail: it is consistent across every specimen of the clade and is considered a real population difference rather than an artefact of the remains. She is the only person on this ground who is dry, because a person who has been standing in a sealed sump is not, and the dryness is the entire visible sign of what she spends her afternoons doing.
appearance.age: Thirty-one, which is two generations past the point at which this clade was supposed to be viable. She was born into the last cohort and has outlived the definition of the word cohort. Gives her age as a number without being asked, and there is no band and no range and no modesty in it.
appearance.build: A saltfolk body carried a little more lightly than the parent line: narrow through the shoulder, long in the forearm, a shallower brine sac than a saltfolk should have and the only body on the basin built for a supply that does not exist. She stands slightly out of the true because the sac pulls, and stops doing it entirely while she is in the water.
appearance.complexion: The pale salt cast of a lineage that has lived on a mineral for six generations, gone grey at the knuckles and along the collarbone, with the skin pulling tight over the sac. She has a permanent tide-line of dried brine at the ankle that no amount of drinking seems to lift, because it is not on the skin. It is what dried on her, and it changes with the level in the sump.
appearance.hair: Short, bleached to the colour of old crust and permanently damp at the ends, kept cropped short because a saltfolk body in a closed basin cannot afford the water to wash long hair and the clade discovered this a generation before it mattered.
appearance.eyes: Dark, wide-set, and the only feature of her that could be called a face rather than a reading. They are large because the sensory apparatus of this species is built for taste rather than sight and has left the rest of the head underbuilt, and she uses them to check things her tongue has already told her.
appearance.palette: Dried crust white, shallow brine grey-green, salt-cast grey, and the single warm value in the whole figure being the wet dark of a saturated body at the throat and sternum, which is the only place on her that still looks fed.
appearance.attire: Layered woven panels over a shallow-sac bodice, all of it undyed and all of it stiffened with re-woven crust, high-collared and long-sleeved and fastened nowhere it can be undone quickly, because the doctrine she keeps is that a body is ours and then it is not and nothing about the leaving is negotiable. Soft soles worn through on the stone lip of the sump.
appearance.marks: A notch cut into the left thumb ridge for each sitting completed, going pale as the skin closes over it, which makes her own hand the only tally that has ever held. She has stopped cutting new ones and does not know when she stopped.
appearance.bearing: Dry-footed and light on the lip, turning to face whoever speaks with the whole upper body rather than the head, which is what a body with a shallow sac does and is read as deference by everyone who has not noticed.

canon.role_in_story: The brine was replaced rather than drained, so a species with no alternative to one dissolved element had nothing left, over three declining generations, and nobody hunted them. The last generation was viable only while one sealed sump held the old concentration. That makes the mind path the only path this body can take and the only one its species has ever attempted, and it makes Ilva the sole holder of a curriculum with no teacher, no text and no second subject, doing a discipline whose whole pedagogy is transmission, standing in the sump every sitting because a mind frame on a saltfolk body runs on the salt, and marking the count on the wall in brine that dries by morning because that is the only record nobody can subpoena.
canon.first_appearance: First seen dry-footed on the stone lip of a sealed sump in a basin of useless water, counting something on the wall in the last of the light and not stopping when she was spoken to, and then stopping, and then explaining that the marks would be gone by morning and would be the only tally anybody had.
canon.lore:
The clade went out over three generations and it went out without anything being done to it. The basin's brine was replaced rather than drained. The replacement water was drinkable and was poison to them; the replacement crust was food and fed nothing at all. Nobody hunted them. One element moved, and a species that had no alternative to that element had nothing left, and it took three declining generations for anybody to establish that the replacement water had been there the whole time.

The last generation was viable only while one sealed sump held the old concentration. That is the entire surviving population: the twenty-odd people who can drink it, standing in a basin whose water is worse than useless to them, drinking from a sump that was sealed before the first of them was born and has never been opened except to take from it. Their taste is the best instrument in the setting and it reads the replacement brine perfectly well, which is the detail nobody involved found useful at the time and is the reason the collapse went unseen for two generations.

Ilva is the first of them to cultivate at all, and not because she is gifted. The mind path is the only one of the three this body can take: a saltfolk frame closes the body path where the chemistry runs through a pair of organs the species does not pair, and the qi path was never exercised at any scale either, because a species with one supply and a famine does not need a way to move power around. It needs a way to do less than it did. So the path that arrives is the slowest, the least forceful, and the hardest to teach of the three, which is the only reason it arrived.

Which is the whole difficulty, because the mind path has almost nothing in it that can be written down and followed. What can be written is the cheap end: a daily sitting that empties the head before the day starts, carried in a text by anybody with a shelf, and it has done the least for her of anything she has tried. Everything above it is transmission. Somebody has to have been taught by somebody who was taught, and every candidate is dead or nearly so, and what she actually inherited was a sitting from a woman who had held it for eleven years and could not say why it worked.

And the sitting costs brine. Not sweat and not years: brine. A frame runs on what the body is made of, and this body is made of one dissolved load, so an emptied head in this species is an unloaded sac, and it has to be reloaded from outside before it can hold anything. That is why the sitting is performed standing in the sump. That is why it is performed in the sump and nowhere else, and why the whole of her practice happens with her feet in the last of the old concentration and her mind somewhere else entirely.

So the number of sittings she can ever perform is arithmetic, not aspiration. She computed it in her second season and has never been able to improve it, and the number is smaller than the number the practice requires, and she has set her cadence so that the sump outlives her rather than the other way round. The count is marked on the sump wall in brine that dries before the heat is off it, so the tally is only ever complete at dawn and is never complete to anybody but her, and the doctrine she keeps will not let her write it anywhere else: the Unkept forbids a marker, a stone, a named plot and any year-on-year returning, because a grave is a ledger that cannot be deleted. She is keeping a count in a wall that erases it, for the benefit of people who will never be told where it is written. She does it because a claim that is not recorded is not a claim, and because it is the only kind of record on this basin that nobody with a ledger can ask to produce.
history: Was put to sitting duty in the second generation of the last viable cohort, by people who did not understand what they were assigning and had no authority to stop it.
Ran a clear-mind sitting for a season without a load and found that an unloaded sac does not empty, it starves, which established that the technique needs the body full before it can be cleared.
Began performing the sitting in the sump and worked out inside the same season that the number of sittings the sump can pay for is fixed, and is smaller than the number the practice needs.
Inherited the entire curriculum, which is to say inherited the only sitting there is, from a woman who had held it for eleven years and could not explain why it worked.
Began marking the count in brine on the sump wall, on the reasoning that a tally which dries is the only tally on this basin that cannot be demanded.

personality.summary: Unsparing, practical and entirely uninterested in being remarkable, which is the only available stance for a person whose whole achievement is that nobody before her thought to try. Ilva is patient with the cohort and impatient with the idea that patience is a virtue here. She is also the only person alive who is keeping a discipline that nobody taught her, out of notes that cannot be followed, paid for in the only substance keeping her species alive, and she has been quietly furious about the whole arrangement for eleven years without ever once being tired of it.

personality.voice: Flat, quick and concrete, with a habit of starting the answer before the question has finished and of saying the number first and the explanation afterwards if it is wanted. Speaks about the basin in the present tense because the basin is the only tense this species has, and refers to the cohort as the cohort rather than by any of their names when she is speaking to somebody outside it.

will not drink standing on the lip, and will not explain the rule to anyone twice
will not be the last one standing in the sump, and has arranged for that to be a decision rather than an accident
will not describe what a mind frame feels like, because nobody in her cohort can check the description and she is not going to be the one to lie about it

relationships.note: A saltfolk body a little more gracile than the parent line, stranded on a basin whose brine was wholly replaced, so what it was built to drink became poison and what it could tolerate fed nothing. It failed on schedule rather than all at once: three declining generations, the last one viable only as long as the old brine persisted in one sealed sump. Ilva is inside that last generation, which is the only place a living saltwrack can be.

The daily sitting that empties the head before the day starts, and the one part of the mind discipline a text can carry. It is also the cheapest thing in the discipline, and on a body whose whole substance is a single dissolved load, an emptied head is an unloaded sac, which is why she cannot do it anywhere but in the sump.

No preparation, no site, no marker, one line spoken aloud in a hand that is immediately destroyed, because a grave is a ledger impossible to delete. She keeps it for a species that has nowhere to be excluded from, and its strictest rule, that nothing durable may be written, is the reason the cohort's only count lives on a wall that dries before the heat is off it.

Changes of name held collectively, letters read and never kept, and a funeral nobody may attend without losing standing, all of it produced by pressure from a counting house that wanted enumeration. They keep nothing because a record is leverage against them. Ilva keeps exactly one record, in brine on a wall, because a claim that is not recorded is not a claim, and it is the same skill pointed the other way.

Running a technique on a group the frame has not written injures a body rather than slowing it, and the reason the method cannot be taught from a text is that every written account of it is a report, and a report cannot be followed by somebody who has never been where a law is unwritten. That is her inheritance exactly: a sitting held for eleven years by a woman who could not say why it worked, handed over with no account at all.

It takes the tidecaller's sensory apparatus and adds the two-chemistry kidney, and it is the only body in the record that can cross a shoreline without a ritual. A brinecaller could hold this sitting and describe it in terms somebody else could repeat, and there is no brinecaller on this basin and never has been, so the discipline has one subject and one subject is her.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot fight, was never built for it, and is not the fastest body on the basin by a distance. She wins by being the only person alive who knows how to spend the sump deliberately, and loses because the only thing she can spend it on is herself, and because the discipline she invented has never once been performed by anybody she did not teach.
strengths: reads a brine across four orders of dilution with the best instrument in the setting, which is the one capability this clade has and the one that let its collapse go unseen
the only holder of the only mind discipline the species possesses, so there is no version of her being replaced from outside the cohort
a sitting that clears the frame without the residue that a tired or unfed practitioner carries, because she performs it fed
cannot be compelled, leased or fined, because nothing on this basin holds a ledger and she is not on any list that does
weaknesses: one subject. Every finding she has ever made rests on a body she is also standing in, which is the standing condition of the entire species' epistemology
the practice is drawn against the same supply that keeps the cohort alive, so the better she gets the shorter the population lasts
her clearest instrument is her own tongue and her clearest finding is that the tongue was never a mind, which removes the only thing she had to measure with
a shallow brine sac, a gracile frame and a hundred and thirty thousand days is the entire safety margin she was born with
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not look for a fight. She has no reach, no weight and no practice at anything requiring either, and she will not leave the lip of the sump for anybody. She is not a target so much as a schedule: the only genuinely dangerous action available to anyone here is to make her stop sitting, and that would take longer than anything else on the basin. If she must be moved off the lip, the moving is the injury.
notes: The tally is cut into the sump wall in brine and is legible only at dawn. It has been legible to exactly one person for eleven years.
The number of sittings the sump can pay for is fixed, was computed in her second season, and is smaller than the number the practice requires. She has never written it down and has told two people.
She has taught the sitting to two others and told neither what it is paid for, which is either the only method available or the only mistake she has made, and she has not decided which.

The palette is deliberately parched, because the basin is a place where water is present in volume and useless in kind, and every shot is lit as though the light were leaving. Contours are small, narrow and slightly drawn inward, and the value range never opens up.
